_about: Layer materials for the assembly builder. R-values are hr-ft2-F/Btu (per inch where stated). Every value names its source. Two entries (loose-fill cellulose and vermiculite) are still marked 'estimated' because no open source for them could be reached; data/README.md explains. Enter a measured or rated value in the house file when one is known.

materials.name: Gypsum board (drywall)
materials.source: OpenStudio-HPXML materials.rb (commit fb18723), conductivity k converted to R per inch = 1/k

materials.name: Plaster on wood lath
materials.source: Sum of two sourced parts: 5/8 in gypsum plaster at 80 lb/ft3, R-0.20 (NREL openstudio-standards, ashrae_90_1.materials.json (entries marked 'From CEC Title24 2013', the California Energy Commission's Title 24 2013 materials list): 'Gypsum plaster - 80 lb/ft3 - 5/8 in.', k = 3.2004 Btu-in/h-ft2-F), plus 1/4 in softwood lath at R-1.249 per inch = R-0.31 (OpenStudio-HPXML materials.rb, wood k = 0.8004)
materials.note: Three-coat plaster over wood lath, about 7/8 in total. No published value for the combination was found; it is built from its two layers.

materials.name: Plaster on metal lath
materials.source: NREL openstudio-standards, ashrae_90_1.materials.json (entries marked 'From CEC Title24 2013', the California Energy Commission's Title 24 2013 materials list): 'Gypsum plaster - on metal lath 80 lb/ft3 - 3/4 in.', R = 0.234

materials.name: Board sheathing (3/4 in, straight or diagonal)

materials.name: Closed air space (empty framed cavity)
materials.source: OpenStudio-HPXML materials.rb Material.AirCavityClosed (R-1.0 for any enclosed gap)
materials.note: An uninsulated stud or joist cavity closed on both sides.

materials.name: Fiberglass batt
materials.source: EnergyPlus dataset ASHRAE_2005_HOF_Materials.idf (U.S. DOE, EnergyPlus repository, datasets/), which reproduces ASHRAE Handbook of Fundamentals 2005, chapter 25, table 4: 'Mineral fiber - processed from rock, slag, or glass - 75-100mm', R = 1.94 m2-K/W = R-11.0, taken over a 3.5 in cavity
materials.note: This is the common R-11 batt in a 3.5 in cavity. Higher-density batts are rated up to R-15 for the same depth: enter the rated R-value of the layer when known.

materials.name: Mineral wool batt
materials.source: EnergyPlus dataset ASHRAE_2005_HOF_Materials.idf (U.S. DOE, EnergyPlus repository, datasets/), which reproduces ASHRAE Handbook of Fundamentals 2005, chapter 25, table 4: 'Mineral fiber - processed from rock, slag, or glass - 90mm - 19-26 kg/m3' (high-density batt), R = 2.63 m2-K/W = R-14.9 over 3.54 in

materials.name: Cellulose, dense-packed in a closed cavity
materials.source: NREL openstudio-standards, ashrae_90_1.materials.json (entries marked 'From CEC Title24 2013', the California Energy Commission's Title 24 2013 materials list): 'Spray applied - Cellulosic fiber - 4.6 lb/ft3', k = 0.3204 Btu-in/h-ft2-F
materials.note: Source value is for cellulose installed at 4.6 lb/ft3; dense-pack wall fill is typically 3.5 to 4 lb/ft3.

materials.name: Cellulose, loose fill (attic floor)
materials.source: Typical published value written from memory: no open source for it could be reached from the build environment (only GitHub-hosted DOE/NREL data files were reachable), see data/README.md [CONFIRM]

materials.name: Fiberglass, loose fill (attic floor)
materials.source: EnergyPlus dataset ASHRAE_2005_HOF_Materials.idf (U.S. DOE, EnergyPlus repository, datasets/), which reproduces ASHRAE Handbook of Fundamentals 2005, chapter 25, table 4: loose fill 'Mineral fiber (rock, slag, glass) - 95-130mm', R = 1.94 m2-K/W = R-11.0 at the 4.4 in midpoint depth

materials.name: Vermiculite, loose fill
materials.source: Typical published value written from memory: no open source for it could be reached from the build environment (only GitHub-hosted DOE/NREL data files were reachable), see data/README.md [CONFIRM]
materials.note: Often found in older attics; may contain asbestos.

materials.source: NREL openstudio-standards, ashrae_90_1.materials.json (entries marked 'From CEC Title24 2013', the California Energy Commission's Title 24 2013 materials list): 'Spray applied - Polyurethane foam - 3.0 lb/ft3', k = 0.20004 Btu-in/h-ft2-F
materials.note: Products are often rated higher (R-6 or more per inch when new). Enter the rated R-value of the layer when known.

materials.note: Foil-faced boards are usually rated R-6 to R-6.5 per inch: enter the rated R-value when known.
